I thought *Idle Slayer* was just going to be another simple idle game where you click a few buttons, watch numbers go up, and forget about it.

I was wrong.

At first, it looks incredibly simple. You run through a pixel-art world, collect coins, defeat enemies, and buy upgrades.

Then you realize you've been playing for three hours.

The game does something surprisingly clever with the idea of an idle game. You can actively play, jumping around, collecting resources, and fighting enemies, but you can also let your progress continue while you're away.

And somehow, both sides of the game work.

The progression is probably the most addictive part. You start with almost nothing, slowly unlock upgrades, discover new mechanics, and eventually realize just how much there is hiding behind what initially looks like a simple platformer.

Then you unlock something new.

Then another thing.

Then

One of the deepest Idle games out there, starts off rather well, keeps going pretty good till you discover the village.
Then it opens into some brand new toys. Never expected such a far array of activities, upgrades and other powerups you can do in a free to play idler. 
There are of course, premium upgrade options like there always are in freetoplays but theyre really unnecessary to progress.
You can grind up about everything with enough time, the walls in progress are also pretty simple to overcome with classic idle powerup comboes you find in other games.

All in all I could recommend it if you have the patience to get to the really juicy part of the game.

reviews.title: Interesting but Confusing
reviews.text:
Compelling game loop with interesting concepts but the further I play the less the math actually seems to work as it’s described.

Something will claim to offer a bonus of some flat percentage per achievement or something like that. But it’s all actually just additive to whatever the miserable base income is. No stacking multiplicatives. The descriptions of each bonus to your equipment is handled the same way. 100% bonus? Nahhh it’s just another multiplier added to the base value. It really might as well actually just say “increased to x2 from x3” the percentages are distracting and annoying and only serve to smokescreen what the maths actually are. Exponential growth works very differently.

You could spend weeks upgrading your ascension tables only to still be bogged down in the nonillions of income, essentially getting nowhere.

One of the only issues I’ve had with it is that there seems to be a huge wall after you buy the ambidextrous upgrade to unlock gloves but after a couple more upgrades they seem to get too expensive. For example I’m at 71.9 Sp  coins per second but the next upgrade I need costs 25 No so I haven’t been able to pass this one spot even after ascending close to ten times. I know the devs do a great job listening to the community and you’re doing a great job with your game please keep up the good work thank you.

reviews.title: Super Fun Game!!!
reviews.text: So I saw this on an add for TikTok and was like “oh I bet it’s like all the other apps advertised on TikTok” that are “free and fun” but are actually “free and fun for the first couple of missions then it’s every time you finish a mission it ‘would you like to double triple or times 5 your reward?’” And if you hit no thanks it’s like “well to bad your watching a video anyways even without a reward” but no this game is actually free and fun sure there’s in app purchases but you don’t need to buy them to have fun. 10/10 would recommend this game. Thank you developers for making a fun and free phone game!!!! Can’t wait to see what the future holds!!!!!

reviews.title: I don’t normally write reviews but this games deserves one
reviews.text: I had originally downloaded this game looking for something to grind while I’m at work but wow this game is top tier. The progression in this game is so deep. Yeah the game gets grindy but actively playing can circumvent a lot of the grind. You set your own pace, you decide which upgrades you want, every play through is different. If you’re lost while playing, check out the wiki. It’s got a ton of good information and guides. Also this is an entirely free game and you don’t even have to watch ads. Have fun! And big thanks to the developer for adding cross saves for pc and phone. You da real mvps.

reviews.title: From a idle snob, this game is caviar!
reviews.text: A latecomer in finding this game, but wow…just wow.  I play a lot of idle rpgs, idle factories, shape crushing, tycoon, crafting, mining, space exploration, etc.  A common problem is that the games become anything but idle.  With pvp, timed events, voluminous IAP’s that guarantee you will max out your play.  This game has a simple no-ads option at a fair price, and anything else is non-critical.  If you play for hours or else once a week, either way you miss out on nothing.  You get out of it the play you put into it.  It’s retro feel is great, it’s playability is relaxing (one-handed!).  The devs are really tuned in to what works.  Thanks.

reviews.title: Good game but...
reviews.text: I paid for the $3.99 bonus to get 50x coins, right? Then after about 5 minutes of that I hit a bonus stage where you jump over pits, as soon as my head hits the bonus stage block to get teleported there the game crashes. I join back in to see that I’m not in the bonus stage anymore and also... 7 minutes of my boost was taken away for NOTHING. Meaning I spent my money on basically nothing. reviews.title: Good idle game, with a twist
reviews.text:
The twist is that while the majority of the gameplay is a pretty high quality version of what you’ve probably come to expect from idle games, there is a “bonus” level that comes up occasionally that is a sort of platforming challenge and it will make you want to claw your eyes out and jump out of a plane. You can skip it but pretty quickly that will forcibly halt your progress until you run this rare “bonus” event about 12 times, presumably more later, and so you’ll struggle to time tight jumps with unresponsive controls and a character who loves randomly jumping higher or farther than normal. 

Otherwise great game.

reviews.title: Very solid game
reviews.text:
First off I’d like to say that I’ve been playing this game for a little over 100 days, and despite me not being active for some of them I am still drawn to play this game in my free time. 

Developer involvement is phenomenal to say the least, and it is made very clear that Pablo has a passion for this game. I am usually incredibly frugal about spending money on free games, but I was so enthralled in Idle Slayer I did end up buying the Anti-Ad feature. This says a lot because if I were drawn to spend money on a mobile game it must mean that I really enjoy it.

Unlike most free mobile games and especially idle ones, ads are not showed down the players throat and remain completely optional. This is a step in the right direction and I hope it remains this way in the future.

To conclude this game is a great time killer and clearly has a bright future ahead of it. I wish nothing but the best

reviews.title: A Nice Change From Idle Games
reviews.text: This game is absolutely incredible. You can really feel the love and attention that went into the creation of this game. The gameplay is also super fun and replayable, but my favorite part is how it relieves some of the frustration from other idle games. You’re not overwhelmed with options, you always feel like you are making steady progress, you aren’t punished for actually playing the game, and it makes me keep coming back. If you want a fun mobile game that you can sit back and relax while playing, this game is for you.

reviews.title: Probably the best idle out there!

I have no problems at all with this game, but it would be hard to fine one considering how amazing it is. Even now, after getting the game a little after launch, I find myself enthralled in the game. reviews.title: Great game!

reviews.title: Has great potential but terrible gameplay
reviews.text: Alright hear me out here; I understand it’s a clicker game but the way it’s designed makes it clear that it is geared to be slightly more. They have a great framework worked out with abilities and skills and even entirely different dimensions with great backgrounds and tile art, but I feel like all of this is wasted with its terrible gameplay; the enemies are all instakills aside from the giants which are hardly more and the coin, enemy, and tile patterns repeat about every ten seconds which makes it terribly mundane and repetitious. I hope to see the devs continue to improve and make it a great game since I have every bit of confidence it can get there with some simple balances and improvements to gameplay.

reviews.title: Great game, however…
reviews.text:

Unfortunately, the newest update to v4.2.1 has a game breaking bug in it. I can no longer play. After the game loads to 100%, it freezes and crashes. Never had any issues prior.
I hope they fix it because I’ve invested a lot of time in the game.
I still recommend this game, and hopefully the bug doesn’t affect you.

reviews.title: Been Playing For 3.5 Years
reviews.text:

Lots of unlocks and things to level.  Huge talent tree, upgrades, minions and divinities, gear to craft and level, daily and weekly quests and you build a village.  

The game gives you enough chances to get free gems. You wont feel pressured to buy anything.  The ads are not intrusive however if you are serious about playing, pay for no ads.

It took me a week, well over 14 hours of in game time, but perhaps you might think like I did, that a dark demon would be a dark type, and that it would all be worthwhile.  You see at this point in the game, you get +100% extra rewards for killing dark types. For an idle game, this seems like such a good goal to work towards does it not?

reviews.title: Definitely an above average idle game.
reviews.text:

The only two negatives I can think of that bothered me was, there seems to be a huge roadblock in progressing around 300k-500k souls area with 75-85ish percent of the upgrades bought.  Trying to get the gauntlet past 150 felt daunting. Also the crafting would be a bit better imo, if the temporary bonuses were a bit larger, they didn’t feel worth getting vs the permanent upgrades.

I also recommend the no ads option. Definitely worth the few bucks if you’re into idlers.

reviews.title: Major flaw
reviews.text:
Game is enjoyable, and felt well balanced until ascension, when the game’s major flaw was revealed. 

There is absolutely no correlation between money earned and ascension points. Ascension points are awarded based on number of enemies killed. The rate that you accumulate ascension points does not change. After the first ascension, you can progress through the game without ever upgrading anything but the ascension board if you select the Soul Gatherer Bundle perk. 

Making your entire skill tree obsolete after the first ascension seems like a pretty glaring oversight.

reviews.title: Pretty good

reviews.title: Not your average Idle game
reviews.text: This has been the most fun idle game. Ever. It almost feels like you’re not actually playing an idle game. The hundreds of achievements to collect, tons of unlockable content, and lastly it actually takes you days/weeks to progress in the late stage of the game. 10/10 would recommend to anyone who wants something casual.

reviews.title: We are cared about
reviews.text: I don’t know where to start. I’ve been playing this game for 3ish years and I love it. Ever since I started I knew that the developer cares more about the players than the revenue. This game is fun and a good time consumer. Most importantly it’s fair to the player, and never a pay to win. Thanks to the developer for making such an awesome game.

reviews.title: Some Ideas for the Dev
reviews.text:
Loving the game and close to 100%.
It would be very satisfying to see the upgrades show up on our character.
(I can do pixel art if you’re interested)
More options when upgrading would be nice like a separate skill tree for another type of currency like the gems or souls.
It would even be okay if they just cost gold because the progression comes to a somewhat substantial halt after you reset a few times. 
More mini games would be very nice or at least some more variety with the existing one mostly for more money / soul making opportunities.
I’ve been loving the game so far!
Great work Dev keep it up.

reviews.title: What I needed
reviews.text: This game satisfies my insatiable desire to play a mobile game. You grind and grind and grind and then go back and start over. I've been playing for months and I'm still not finished. reviews.title: Anti-idle slayer
reviews.text:
Decent game, but hardly an idle game. You have offline progress, which is super slow, or you have to be super active while game is open. Early on it’s fine since it doesn’t take a long time with active gameplay to make progress. After multiple
 ascensions however, you have to play active for a very long time just get 1 small upgrade. Game needs to have an actual idle system where you can have game open and it runs, jumps, and shoots automatically.

reviews.title: Perfectly Executed
reviews.text:
I don’t usually like idle games, but I have enjoyed this game. What I enjoy most and really think is the main pull for me is the art. It is essentially a pixel art gallery where you have to wait for the coin to see the next piece. I love pixel art.

The programming is flawless.

I only wish developers would leave out the mystical content such as the Soul Gatherer in these type of games. 

Otherwise, it is the best version of this type of game I have tried.

I’m still hoping that one day a developer with these skills will make a casual style Lord of the Rings game with this type of art. I would pay loads for that.

reviews.title: Has gambling mechanic
reviews.text: This game would be a decent time waster except for the chest hunt mini “game”. It’s just a gambling mechanic that doesn’t add anything good to the game. Would not recommend this game simply because of that. Edit: there’s a slot machine and roulette that hold more necessary upgrades. Any bonuses are lost upon closing the game which is about as dumb as it sounds for an idle game on a mobile device to remove all in game bonuses if you lock your device. I could pick this game apart till there’s nothing left. Just find something better.

reviews.title: IN LOVE

reviews.title: Dark patterns, the game
reviews.text:
Highly addictive and is absolutely filled with dark patterns. I feel gross after playing this. The gameplay barely exists, the bonus stages are uninspired, and most of the upgrades are just variants of “get x% more coins”.
If you like watching numbers get bigger, you’ll love it. If you want to actually engage your brain, look elsewhere. This is barely a game. 

Don’t buy any of the currency they shove in your face, and don’t pay to turn off the optional ads.
